speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Your history of ulcerative colitis and high-risk sexual behavior raises concern for specific infections. Have you noticed any skin rashes, fever, or weight loss in the last two months?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC).

The presence of scleral icterus, severe pruritus, and a history of ulcerative colitis strongly suggests an autoimmune etiology affecting the bile ducts. I am requesting your Anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA) test results and liver imaging to confirm the diagnosis.
